description: Live demo: Redis cache invalidation by keyspace scan versus a per-entity index, measured under load in Docker.

userStories.title: Compose skeleton, Redis, and the shared toolchain
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `make up` to bring up Redis and a health-checkable workspace so every later story has somewhere to land.
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml defines the `redis` service on 6379 with `--maxmemory-policy noeviction --save '' --appendonly no`
Root package.json declares npm workspaces: services/test-api, services/webhook, services/benchmark, packages/cache
Root tsconfig.base.json sets strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, target ES2022, module commonjs
Makefile provides: up, down, logs, typecheck, test, seed, reset, verify
`make up` starts Redis and `redis-cli -h localhost ping` returns PONG
`make typecheck` runs and exits 0 (no services yet is fine)
README section 'Quick start' documents make up / make seed / open localhost:3000

userStories.title: packages/cache — the shared entity index
userStories.description: As a developer, I need one tested TypeScript module implementing both the index and its invalidation, so test-api and webhook cannot drift apart.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cache exports EntityIndexCacheStrategy with: indexKeyFor, parse, register, invalidateEntities, prune
register uses MULTI: SADD, then EXPIRE key ttl NX, then EXPIRE key ttl GT — and inspects every reply tuple
invalidateEntities order is SMEMBERS then UNLINK values then SREM the observed members — never DEL the set
invalidateEntities deletes every recorded member unconditionally; it must not filter by any timestamp
All multi-key commands are batched (default 500); no spread of an unbounded array
TTLs validated as whole seconds 1..2592000 BEFORE any write
Unit tests cover: NX+GT actually sets and extends an expiry; a failed UNLINK leaves the index intact and a retry completes; SREM preserves a concurrently added member
`make typecheck` and `make test` both exit 0

userStories.title: test-api service
userStories.description: As the benchmark, I need an innocent bystander service reading the cache, so the blocking effect of a scan is observable from outside the scanning process.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /entitlement/:userId returns {userId,hit,variants,latencyMs} per docs/API.md
It reads via SMEMBERS then MGET. It never calls KEYS or SCAN
latencyMs measures only the Redis round trip, using process.hrtime.bigint()
The service opens its OWN Redis connection, not shared with any other service
GET /health returns {ok:true}
Dockerfile builds; the service is in docker-compose.yml on 3001 with a healthcheck
`curl localhost:3001/health` returns ok after `make up`
`make typecheck` exits 0

userStories.title: webhook service with both invalidation paths
userStories.description: As the demo, I need the legacy and indexed eviction paths side by side behind two endpoints, so the graph can compare them under identical conditions.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/invalidate and POST /v2/invalidate both accept {userIds:[...]} and return 202 {jobId,mode,total} IMMEDIATELY
v1 runs KEYS *::<userId>::* per user then deletes the matches — the pattern must not match the index key
v2 delegates to packages/cache invalidateEntities
Work runs in the background; GET /jobs/:id reports {state,total,processed,removed}
POST /jobs/:id/stop aborts between users and sets state to stopped
GET /health returns {ok:true}; service is in compose on 3002 with a healthcheck
An integration test seeds ~200 keys, runs v1 and v2 on disjoint users, and asserts both remove every cache key for their users
`make typecheck` and `make test` exit 0

userStories.title: benchmark service — deterministic seeder
userStories.description: As a user, I need the fixture generated reproducibly from a seed so runs are comparable and nothing large lives in git.
acceptanceCriteria: Seeding is deterministic from SEED_VALUE: the same seed produces byte-identical keys and values
Each user gets 1..3 variants; SEED_KEYS (default 2000000) is the number of CACHE RECORDS
Writes cache strings with TTL 3600 AND the matching index sets, using pipelines of ~20k commands
Every pipeline reply is inspected; any error aborts seeding and sets state failed
On completion it asserts DBSIZE equals the expected total and stores a marker key so restarts do not reseed
GET /api/seed/status and POST /api/seed and POST /api/seed/reset behave per docs/API.md
Progress is emitted over WebSocket as {t:'seed-progress'} frames at least once a second
`make seed` completes for SEED_KEYS=50000 in under 30 seconds and status becomes ready
`make typecheck` exits 0

userStories.title: benchmark service — run driver
userStories.description: As a user, I need a run to poll test-api every second and fire the eviction batch a second later, so the graph shows a clean before and after.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/run {mode:'v1'|'v2'} starts polling test-api once per POLL_INTERVAL_MS with a random seeded user id
After BATCH_DELAY_MS it POSTs BATCH_USERS ids (default 1000) to the matching webhook endpoint and records the returned jobId
Users sent for eviction are drawn from the seeded id space so they always exist
Each poll produces a {t:'sample'} WebSocket frame including latencyMs and the webhook job counters
POST /api/run/stop stops polling AND calls the webhook stop endpoint
Only one run may be active; a second POST /api/run returns 409
A client connecting mid-run first receives a {t:'history'} frame with the samples so far
Integration test with SEED_KEYS=50000 asserts a v2 run completes and emits samples
`make typecheck` and `make test` exit 0

userStories.title: benchmark service — live UI
userStories.description: As a user, I want one page with a real-time chart and three buttons so the difference is visible without reading any code.
acceptanceCriteria: GET / serves a single self-contained HTML page — no build step, no CDN dependency required to render the chart
A time-series chart updates once per second from the WebSocket, x = seconds since run start, y = latencyMs on a LOG scale
A log scale is required: the two modes differ by ~4 orders of magnitude and a linear axis makes v2 invisible
Buttons: 'Measure legacy (KEYS) eviction', 'Measure hashed index eviction', and 'Stop'
A marker or shaded band shows the moment the eviction batch was dispatched
A status strip shows seed state, key count, run mode, and webhook job progress
If the fixture is not seeded the run buttons are disabled and a Seed button is shown instead
The page reconnects the WebSocket automatically and redraws from the history frame
Verified in a browser: both runs start, the chart moves, Stop halts it

userStories.title: End-to-end verification and documentation
userStories.description: As a visitor to the repo, I need one command that proves the whole thing works, and a README that shows the result.
acceptanceCriteria: `make verify` brings the stack up, seeds SEED_KEYS=50000, runs v2 end to end, asserts the target users' keys are gone, and exits non-zero on any failure
README documents: quick start, the two runs and what each graph should look like, memory and timing expectations, and the honest caveats from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
README states that a 1000-user v1 batch is not meant to finish, and why
README links docs/REDIS-SCHEMA.md, docs/API.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/BENCHMARK-BASELINE.md
A screenshot or captured sample output of each run is committed under docs/
`make typecheck`, `make test` and `make verify` all exit 0 from a clean clone

userStories.title: Cache strategies, the @Cache adapter, and a lazily-filled fixture
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the cache reached through a @Cache decorator over a strategy hierarchy, so a service caches a method by annotating it and never builds a key by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cache exports DefaultCacheStrategy with a protected readonly RedisClient shared with subclasses, and async get(key) / set(key,value,ttlSeconds); set validates the TTL before issuing any command
EntityIndex is renamed EntityIndexCacheStrategy everywhere (packages, services, tests, docs, prd.json) with NO compatibility alias; `grep -rn '\bEntityIndex\b'` finds no matches

EntityIndexCacheStrategy extends DefaultCacheStrategy and overrides set(): a key whose category it does not own falls back to super.set(); a key it owns goes through registerMany([{cacheKey,value,ttlSeconds}]) so SET EX and SADD are one MULTI, with a comment saying why super.set() is not called on that path
packages/cache exports enums CacheKey (values are the category segment), TTL (MEDIUM = 3600) and CacheStrategy (DEFAULT, ENTITY_INDEX_CACHE)
configureCache({redis,service,tenant,categories}) registers one instance per strategy; a decorated method called before configureCache throws a clear error and never silently bypasses the cache
@Cache(cacheKey, ttl, strategy) is a standard TypeScript 5 decorator; experimentalDecorators and reflect-metadata are NOT used
The decorator builds service::tenant::category::entityId::params from the first argument and a canonical sorted-key JSON of the rest, and the key round-trips through parse() unchanged
On a hit the underlying method is not called; on a miss the result is written via strategy.set()
Concurrent misses for the same key in one process collapse to a single underlying call (single-flight)
A method that throws is never cached and writes nothing; an undefined result is not cached; a null result is cached only under an explicit cacheNegative option that defaults to false

services/benchmark gains a deterministic BillingProvider mock producing exactly the fixture generator's record for a given userId, with ORIGIN_LATENCY_MS and ORIGIN_FAIL_USER, and it never touches Redis
A SubscriptionService method decorated @Cache(CacheKey.ACTIVE_SUBSCRIPTION, TTL.MEDIUM, CacheStrategy.ENTITY_INDEX_CACHE) calls BillingProvider.getActiveSubscription(userId)

SEED_MODE=bulk (default) keeps today's pipelined seeding; SEED_MODE=lazy fills every record through the decorator with LAZY_CONCURRENCY (default 16) and refuses above LAZY_MAX_KEYS (default 50000) with an error naming the flag
In both modes the seeder then lazily fills LAZY_WARM_USERS (default 1000) through the decorator as a reported 'lazy-warm' phase, targeting the same users the eviction batch uses
Seeding the same SEED_VALUE in bulk and in lazy produces the same DBSIZE and byte-identical values and TTLs for a sampled key
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md gains a 'cache strategies' section; docs/REDIS-SCHEMA.md and README.md reflect the rename and the new environment variables
`make up` still seeds 2,000,000 records in about a minute; `make typecheck && make test && make verify` exit 0
userStories.notes: Full specification: tasks/US-010.md. Lands before US-009.

userStories.title: test-api read path — read-through cache, fake origin, interleaving test
userStories.description: As a reader of the write-up, I need the demo to fill the cache as well as evict it, so the fill-versus-invalidation race is demonstrable instead of only described.
acceptanceCriteria: test-api gains GET /subscription/:userId returning {userId,source:'cache'|'origin',variants,latencyMs,subscription}; originMs is present when source is 'origin'
The route reads and fills through US-010's @Cache decorator; no second decorator or standalone readThrough() is introduced
A failing origin returns 502 and NOTHING is written to Redis — no value, no index member
GET /entitlement/:userId is unchanged; test-api still never calls KEYS or SCAN
An integration test asserts a fill in flight across an invalidation leaves value and reference consistent and the value surviving to its TTL
An integration test asserts an invalidation after a completed fill removes both value and reference
An integration test asserts an origin error caches nothing and the next call still reaches the origin
docs/API.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (a 'read path' section) and README.md are updated; ARCHITECTURE states the test demonstrates bounded staleness, not atomicity
`make typecheck && make test` exit 0 and `make verify` still exits 0
userStories.notes: Full specification: tasks/US-009.md. Depends on US-010 (the cache API).

userStories.title: mock-billing service, the S2S read chain, and no return await
userStories.description: As a reader of the demo, I need the third party to be a real service behind a network hop, so the cache sits in front of something that can be slow, fail, and speak someone else's schema.
acceptanceCriteria: services/mock-billing exists as a fourth workspace on port 3003 with its own Dockerfile, compose service and healthcheck

It exposes GET /health returning {ok:true,seedValue} and GET /subscription/:userId?v=n returning a snake_case Chargebee-shaped envelope; 404 for an absent variant, 503 for ORIGIN_FAIL_USER, 400 for a userId not matching ^u_\d{7}$
Every field of the envelope derives from @redis-hash-index/fixture's deterministic generator; the same userId, SEED_VALUE and variant always produce the same envelope
mock-billing does not depend on @redis-hash-index/cache and never opens a Redis connection

packages/fixture contains only prng, fixture, schema and its index; billing-provider.ts moved to mock-billing and subscription-service.ts moved to test-api; packages/fixture no longer imports @redis-hash-index/cache
packages/fixture exports one serializeSubscription() used by BOTH the bulk seeder and test-api's mapper, so bulk and lazy values are byte-identical

test-api gains src/billing-client.ts: an S2S client with an AbortController timeout (BILLING_TIMEOUT_MS, default 5000) that maps the envelope to the internal Subscription, turns every non-2xx, timeout, parse failure and connection refusal into OriginError, and maps 404 to null

test-api owns src/subscription-service.ts with @Cache(CacheKey.ACTIVE_SUBSCRIPTION, TTL.MEDIUM, CacheStrategy.ENTITY_INDEX_CACHE); it takes SubscriptionOrigin by constructor so tests inject a stub and open no socket

GET /subscription/u_XXXXXXX?v=n reaches getActiveSubscription(userId,{v:n}) and produces a cache key byte-identical to the bulk seeder's for that record; query parameters outside the key contract never enter the params segment
An OriginError is never cached and the route answers 502; a 404-derived null is not cached; test-api still never calls KEYS or SCAN

The benchmark's lazy and lazy-warm phases fill by calling test-api over HTTP (GET {TEST_API_URL}/subscription/:userId?v=n) with LAZY_CONCURRENCY, and no longer construct a SubscriptionService in process
Bulk seeding is unchanged and `make up` still writes 2,000,000 records in about a minute; ORIGIN_LATENCY_MS and ORIGIN_FAIL_USER are removed from the benchmark service and set on mock-billing
Before its first lazy request the seeder compares mock-billing's /health seedValue with its own and refuses the seed, naming both values, when they differ
docker-compose orders startup: test-api depends on mock-billing healthy; benchmark depends on test-api and mock-billing healthy
`grep -rn 'return await' packages services` matches only the try/finally in packages/cache/src/index.test.ts; functions left with no await are no longer async
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/API.md, docs/REDIS-SCHEMA.md, README.md and .env.example reflect the fourth service, the fill chain and the new variables
A test seeds one user in bulk, invalidates it, refills it through the chain, and asserts the stored string is byte-identical to the bulk value
`make typecheck && make test && make verify` exit 0

userStories.title: Retire /entitlement, and mark the end of the eviction on the chart
userStories.description: As a reader of the demo, I need one endpoint per entity and a chart that shows when the eviction finished, not only when it started.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /entitlement/:userId, its controller handler, its tests and its docs/API.md section are deleted; the internal SMEMBERS+MGET read survives under a name that says what it is

GET /subscription/:userId?fill=false reads the cache without filling it: 200 {userId,source:'cache'|'miss',hit,variants,latencyMs}, no origin call, no scan fallback; fill defaults to true and today's read-through behaviour is unchanged
source:'miss' with hit:false and variants:0 is a 200, not an error — it is the expected state after an eviction; ?v= is ignored in this mode rather than rejected
services/benchmark/src/runner.ts and scripts/verify.mjs both poll GET {TEST_API_URL}/subscription/:userId?fill=false
A test evicts a user, calls the probe repeatedly against the empty cache, and asserts DBSIZE is unchanged and no key or index member was created
Stale /entitlement wording is removed from services/CLAUDE.md and from prd.json's US-003 and US-009 criteria, without changing those stories' passes flags
RunJobCounters carries the webhook job's finishedAt, and the runner emits exactly one batch-completed frame per run when a poll first observes a terminal state
The batch-completed frame carries {t,runId,mode,ts,elapsedSec,state,processed,removed,incomplete} with elapsedSec fractional to 3 decimals, derived from finishedAt and the run's startedAt
The batch-dispatched frame's elapsedSec becomes fractional too, so a fast v2 completion can never render before its dispatch; sample frames keep rounded elapsedSec
Polling continues after completion; the run does not auto-stop
The chart draws a second dashed full-height marker coloured by terminal state: green for done, amber for stopped, red for failed
Its label names the state and the counters: 'eviction completed (N users, M keys)', 'eviction stopped after N of M', 'eviction failed — N entities incomplete'
When the two markers are closer than the first label's width, the second label is drawn on a second row and right-aligned if it would overflow the plot
The chart has a legend covering both markers
HistoryFrame and ActiveRun carry the completion, so a browser connecting or reloading mid-run redraws both markers; the UI clears them on run-started
docs/API.md documents the batch-completed frame; README.md says the two v2 lines nearly coincide and that a v1 run normally shows the amber stopped line
`make typecheck && make test && make verify` exit 0
